recaps.text: Tally Youngblood is fifteen, living in the ugly dormitories of a city where everyone is given an operation at sixteen that makes them beautiful and moves them across the river into New Pretty Town. Three months short of her own birthday she sneaks over the water to a party to find Peris, her oldest friend, who has already turned pretty; he is uncomfortable at the sight of her ugly face and tells her to wait her turn. Escaping the mansion, she meets Shay, an ugly who shares her exact birthday and quickly becomes her closest friend. Shay teaches her to ride a hoverboard, takes her on illegal trips beyond the city limits, and refuses to join the game the other uglies play with the software that predicts what they will look like after surgery. For the first time, Tally hears someone treat the operation as a choice rather than a certainty.

Shay leads Tally out to the Rusty Ruins, the remains of a city from the age before, and admits she has been meeting someone from outside: David, who comes from a settlement of people who never had the operation. Shay urges Tally to run away with her before their birthdays. Tally refuses, unwilling to give up the life she has spent years waiting for, and the two argue bitterly. After one last trick together, Shay leaves the city alone, leaving Tally a note with directions written as a riddle so that nobody else could follow them. Tally keeps the note and reports for her operation on her sixteenth birthday, only to find that she is not being taken to the surgery at all.

Instead of the operation, Tally is delivered to Special Circumstances, a division of the city most uglies believe is a myth, and interviewed by Dr. Cable, a pretty whose surgery has made her frightening rather than lovely. Tally is told she will stay ugly indefinitely unless she follows Shay's directions to the runaway settlement, known as the Smoke, and activates a tracking pendant once she is inside, so that the city can shut the place down. She goes to Peris for help and finds he will not risk anything for her. With no other route to becoming pretty, Tally accepts the assignment, takes the pendant and a survival kit, and sets out alone.

Tally follows the riddled directions across hundreds of miles on a hoverboard, living on packets of dehydrated food and sleeping rough. Misreading one leg of the route, she strays into a vast field of white orchids, and a fire she starts there brings in the city's rangers, who put out the blaze and take her in. They explain that the orchids are an engineered species that escaped and is now smothering every other plant across the continent, a reminder that beauty designed without limits can be ruinous. Re-equipped and refuelled, Tally rides on, growing steadily less certain about what she has agreed to do.

Tally reaches the Smoke and finds a working settlement of runaways who farm, cook, salvage and build for themselves. Shay is delighted to see her and never learns why she came. Tally hides the pendant, takes on the settlement's chores, and discovers that she is good at the work and comfortable among people who simply look ordinary. She grows close to David, who was born outside the cities and has never been operated on, which strains her friendship with Shay. The longer she stays, the harder it becomes to imagine handing the place over to Dr. Cable.

David takes Tally to meet his parents, Maddy and Az, both former city surgeons. They tell her what their own research uncovered: the operation that makes everyone pretty also puts lesions in the brain, leaving people placid, incurious and easy to govern, and that is the real reason the cities perform it. Tally understands that the fog she saw in Peris and in every new pretty was put there deliberately. She decides to stay at the Smoke, and to destroy the tracking pendant by throwing it into a fire, not knowing that heat is precisely what switches it on.

Special Circumstances arrives at dawn. Specials sweep through the settlement, binding the runaways and loading them into hovercars; Maddy and Az are taken along with Shay and most of the others. Tally, who was away from the huts, is caught but breaks free, and David, who had been travelling, returns to find his home destroyed. Tally says nothing about the pendant. The two of them dig out the emergency supplies the Smokies had cached for exactly this situation, and set off for the city to get the prisoners back.

Travelling back, Tally and David pass through the Rusty Ruins, where David explains how the old world collapsed: an engineered bacterium that fed on petroleum spread out of control, and the Rusties' oil-dependent civilization went with it. Reaching the city, they use runaway routes and stolen equipment to get inside Special Circumstances headquarters, where the Smokies are being held for interrogation. They free Maddy and the others and escape by hovercar, but Az is dead, killed during questioning, and Shay has already been operated on and is now a pretty who does not want rescuing.

Maddy has spent years preparing a cure: two pills that could undo the brain damage the operation causes. They have never been tested, and she will not experiment on anyone who cannot consent. Shay, now pretty, is placid, forgiving and entirely uninterested in being changed back, which makes her useless as a volunteer and painful to be near. Tally finally admits to David that she came to the Smoke as an informant and that the pendant she burned is what brought the Specials down on them; he is devastated. To put it right, and because a willing subject is the one thing the cure needs, Tally writes and signs a permission note, returns to the city, and hands herself over to be made pretty so that Maddy's pills can be tried on her.

characters.description: A registered nurse who moves into her brother's San Francisco apartment while pursuing an advanced nursing degree. Practical and self-directed, Tate expects the arrangement to be temporary until her first encounter with the withdrawn pilot across the hall unsettles her plans.
characters.name: Tate Collins

characters.description: An airline pilot and close friend of Tate's brother. Tate first finds Miles intoxicated and collapsed outside the apartment, then discovers that his usual manner is quiet, controlled, and difficult to read. His visible distress suggests a history he refuses to discuss.
characters.name: Miles Archer

characters.description: Tate's older brother, an airline pilot who lets her stay in his apartment. Protective and often away for work, Corbin trusts Miles as a close friend but is wary of the other pilots who show interest in his sister.
characters.name: Corbin Collins

characters.description: An elderly man who works the elevator in Corbin's apartment building and dreams of becoming a pilot. Cap's patient humor and attention make him an easy confidant for Tate as she adjusts to the building and its guarded residents.
characters.name: Cap

characters.description: Miles's fellow pilot and longtime friend. Ian knows Miles well enough to recognize the force of the past beneath his reserve, and he offers loyalty without pressing him to disclose more than he can bear.
characters.name: Ian

characters.description: A girl Miles meets during his final year of high school, six years before Tate's arrival. Rachel is immediately compelling to him, and their attraction grows even as changes in their parents' lives threaten to make it complicated.
characters.name: Rachel

characters.description: Miles's father, a widower beginning a serious relationship six years before the main story. His hope of rebuilding a family brings happiness into the household while creating an unexpected conflict for Miles.
characters.name: Miles's Father

characters.description: Rachel's mother and the woman Miles's father loves. Her relationship with him draws the two teenagers' households together and forces Miles and Rachel to reconsider a bond that began before they understood their parents' intentions.
characters.name: Lisa

characters.description: A married pilot in Corbin's circle who persistently directs unwanted attention toward Tate. His casual disregard for boundaries makes him someone she avoids rather than a possible romantic interest.
characters.name: Dillon

recaps.ending: The full memory Miles has resisted is the death of Clayton, the infant son he had with Rachel. During a drive in heavy rain, their car entered the water. Miles saved Rachel but could not save the baby, and afterward he treated loving anyone as a danger he no longer deserved. After Tate leaves, Miles visits Rachel, now living a stable life with a husband and child. Their conversation allows him to see that neither of them must remain fixed inside the worst event of their lives. He returns to Tate, tells her the truth, and offers the love and future he had forbidden himself. Tate accepts him once his choice is based on honesty rather than rules that keep her at a distance. In the epilogue they are married and have a child. Becoming a father brings Miles fear as well as joy, but he no longer responds by shutting love out; the life he builds with Tate shows that acknowledging grief can coexist with choosing happiness again.
recaps.in_short: Nurse Tate Collins moves in with her pilot brother and begins a sexual relationship with his friend Miles Archer, who insists on two rules: she must not ask about his past or expect a future. Tate agrees but falls in love, while chapters from six years earlier show Miles falling for Rachel just as their parents form a household together. Rachel becomes pregnant, and their son Clayton is born, but the baby dies after Miles's car enters the water during a storm. Miles saves Rachel and thereafter believes that love only creates unbearable loss. His arrangement with Tate becomes painful because he will accept intimacy but not hope. Tate finally leaves rather than continue on those terms. Miles visits Rachel, learns that she has rebuilt her life, and begins forgiving himself. He tells Tate the truth and commits to her. They marry and have a child, with Miles choosing love despite the vulnerability it brings.

recaps.text: Tate Collins moves into the San Francisco apartment of her older brother, Corbin, while working as a nurse and studying for an advanced degree. On arrival she finds a stranger drunk and collapsed outside the door. He is Miles Archer, Corbin's neighbor, close friend, and fellow airline pilot. Miles is distressed enough to cry for someone named Rachel, but when sober he is controlled and remote. Tate is attracted to him despite the difficult introduction. She also befriends Cap, the elderly elevator attendant who hopes to fly one day, and meets Ian, another pilot who shares a long history with Miles. Interwoven chapters begin six years earlier, when an eighteen-year-old Miles meets Rachel at school and experiences an immediate, hopeful attraction unlike the emotional restraint Tate sees in him now.

Tate and Miles repeatedly encounter each other through Corbin and the apartment building. Their attraction becomes explicit, but Miles says he cannot offer a conventional relationship. He proposes a sexual arrangement governed by two conditions: Tate must not ask about his past and must not expect a future with him. She accepts, believing she can keep her feelings within the same limits. Six years earlier, Miles and Rachel discover that his widowed father and her mother, Lisa, are in love and intend to unite their households. What had seemed like a simple first romance is suddenly secret and fraught, yet neither teenager is willing to end it. In the present, Miles's tenderness when his guard drops makes Tate suspect that his rules protect a wound rather than a lack of feeling.

The physical relationship deepens. Miles can be attentive and vulnerable with Tate in private, then restores distance whenever closeness implies commitment. Corbin remains unaware, and Tate is increasingly caught between the terms she accepted and the hope created by Miles's behavior. Cap listens without judging while warning, in his own way, that wanting more cannot be turned off by agreement. In the past, Miles and Rachel continue their relationship after their parents marry, hiding it to avoid damaging the new family. Their bond grows more serious, and the secrecy that protects it also isolates them. The contrast between the open-hearted younger Miles and the closed man Tate knows makes clear that a catastrophic event, not simple disinterest, lies between the two timelines.

Tate admits to herself that she loves Miles, though telling him would violate the emotional boundary on which he insists. Moments that resemble a shared life are followed by sharp withdrawals, and the imbalance begins to hurt more than the intimacy compensates for it. Miles remains loyal to Corbin and serious about his work, but refuses every opening through which Tate might know him fully. Six years earlier, Rachel becomes pregnant. She and Miles decide they want the baby and imagine a future together even though the news threatens to expose their relationship and distress their parents. Their son gives Miles's early hopes a concrete shape, intensifying the question of why the present-day Miles has forbidden himself both love and family.

Miles and Tate can no longer pretend that the arrangement affects them equally. Tate seeks emotional recognition; Miles responds to closeness with panic and sometimes causes pain by treating the rules as more important than what is happening between them. His reaction to children and family reveals fear he will not explain. In the earlier timeline, Miles and Rachel face the consequences of the pregnancy with their parents and prepare for their son, Clayton. The baby is loved, but the narrative's growing sense of disaster connects his existence to the grief Miles has carried into adulthood. Tate understands that compassion for Miles's past does not require her to accept a present in which her own needs are continually denied.

Tate finally says what Miles will not: she loves him and wants a future. He cannot return the words or loosen the rules, even though losing her plainly matters to him. She ends the arrangement rather than remain available only on terms that injure her. Ian confronts Miles with the fact that avoiding love has not healed him, while Cap helps Tate recognize that walking away is not a failure of patience. The past approaches the source of Miles's guilt as his life with Rachel and Clayton is overtaken by a storm and a journey that goes disastrously wrong. In the present, separation leaves Miles with the choice he has avoided for six years: keep treating grief as a permanent sentence, or face the memory and become capable of offering Tate something whole.

Six years earlier, Miles loses control of the car in heavy rain and it enters the water. He gets Rachel out but cannot save their infant son, Clayton. The baby's death destroys the young couple, and Miles turns guilt into a belief that loving anyone will only expose them to similar devastation. After Tate leaves, he seeks out Rachel. She has married, has another child, and has built a life that includes the memory of Clayton without being ruled by it. Her survival and forgiveness help Miles begin to forgive himself. He returns to Tate, finally explains his past, declares his love, and asks for a real future rather than a relationship defined by absence. Tate accepts the changed offer. In the epilogue they are married and have a child of their own. Miles is still marked by grief, but he allows fear and happiness to exist together and chooses the family he once thought he could never risk.

recaps.ending: Max's victory over Unbroken is upheld because the contract restricted Max from advancing before the fight but did not prevent Bob, a separate System consciousness, from initiating the advancement after combat began. The arena pays fifty billion divine points. Max advances again to tier six, while Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, Cordelia, Rakonath, and the bound demon companion each reach tier five. Bob develops alongside Max and remains closely integrated with him. About 1.8 billion divine points remain for defenses, expansion, and reserves. The alliance has only around eleven months before its protection ends, with three approaches still requiring fortification. Its deeper problems remain unresolved: the portal collective brings surveillance and obligations, the hostile syndicate has gone quiet, an ancient power continues to coerce arena sacrifices, and the larger contest involving Bob and the other black skills is still obscure. Max and Tanila's daughter remains away with her Tower party on the three-hundred-year onward journey.
recaps.in_short: As the founders prepare for the end of their protection, Max kills a frost Jotun, sees his daughter complete the Tower, repairs a centaur world infected by an infant world eater, and deepens the alliance's training and civic institutions. A portal collective improves divine-point income but exposes the founders to surveillance. Max then uncovers a pattern of peaceful gods coerced into fatal arena challenges and accepts a vastly dangerous wager against Unbroken, an adaptive captive that has consumed seventeen gods. Fowl finds a loophole allowing Bob to advance Max during the fight. After surviving long enough to activate Consume's domain, Max kills and absorbs Unbroken. The arena upholds the result and pays fifty billion divine points. Max reaches tier six, his six fellow founders reach tier five, and the strengthened alliance begins fortifying for the expiration of its protection in roughly eleven months.

recaps.text: Previously: Max and his companions became gods responsible for allied peoples and multiple worlds. Max shares his life and battles with Bob, the sentient black skill called Consume, while Rakonath is bonded to him as a dragon ally. Max and Tanila have a half-elf daughter whose progress through the Tower has carried her close to its completion. The founders' divine status brings resources and authority, but also makes them participants in a much larger contest among gods. Their worlds remain protected for a limited period, giving the group time to strengthen their people and themselves before outside powers can attack directly.

Max risks another public arena battle to gain the divine points his alliance needs, defeating a frost Jotun world-eater after Bob takes control during the worst of the fight. Consume grants major statistics and abilities, but Max refuses a power that would transform him into a solitary consumer of worlds. At home, Max and Tanila's daughter leads her five-member party through the Tower's final trial. The Tower creates a giant duplicate of her, but the party's equipment and coordination overcome it. The daughter delivers the killing blow and barely survives the reflected damage. Her team then crosses the portal into the next stage of its journey, beginning an enforced separation from the founders that will last three hundred years.

With his daughter gone, Max turns toward the alliance's readiness. He builds a protected underground chamber where gods can train against one another without permanent death. Tanila defeats the bound demon companion in its first match through careful battlefield preparation, and Fowl later defeats Cordelia after revealing that decades of poison-resistance training neutralized her main tactic. A decline in divine-point income draws Max to a neglected centaur world suffering drought, sickness, and deaths. A younger warrior condemns his absence and challenges the local elder. Max investigates instead of punishing the criticism, finding a vast life-draining blight around the world's control panel. He destroys its guardian with Wildfire and learns it was an infant world eater, probably planted deliberately. After activating restorative blessings, Max gives the younger warrior a communication ring and directs him to share leadership with the elder while the world recovers.

The alliance cannot identify who planted the infant world eater, but the incident forces the founders to improve communication and governance across their worlds. Bob defeats Rakonath in training through tactics rather than raw force, while Batrire develops Sensory Control after enduring dangerous fire exercises and reconnecting with her purpose as a protector. On a perpetually dark world, hostile inhabitants and a vampire god block Max from the control panel until Bob uses corruptive death magic. A stronger resident god then negotiates access and agrees to maintain the world's contribution. The encounter confirms that world ownership can bring conflict with resident gods and their allies. The founders respond by planning expansion, exploration, dragon relocation, and stronger institutions. Tanila continues difficult rune research, while Max urges patience and makes time for their marriage. He also offers Bob control of his body for ordinary experience rather than only emergencies.

Bob accepts Max's offer and spends time in the capital through Max's body, helping a struggling food seller and recovering a fragment of erased memory. Fowl and Batrire establish a dwarf-led Tower academy as a lasting civic legacy. Meanwhile, a suspicious arena match ends with a water-based god killing a fire-based opponent in a carefully prepared act of revenge. The founders conclude that the arena may be shaping contests rather than serving as a neutral venue. Max uses a demon king's outstanding debt to demand an explanation of the wider divine game. The demon king describes many simultaneous contests with shifting rules, transferable assets, and victories that can be appropriated. He also says the three black skills appear on every active board, but refuses further disclosure without a pact. The debt ends with the founders convinced they need alliances, practice, and a concealed central objective, even though they still do not understand the true game.

At the midpoint of their protection period, the founders accept that ordinary income is unlikely to carry them all to tier five. They weigh costly skill and equipment improvements while pursuing specialized preparation. Rakonath deals with missing young dragons and internal opposition to cooperation with other peoples. Max and Tanila's daughter, now beyond the Tower, governs alongside her multiracial team and remains in contact with her mother. Batrire develops magical perception, defensive healing, and faster recovery from curses. Fowl subjects himself to dragonfire, venom, and petrification to build resistances, planning to add a safeguard against one fatal blow. Cordelia retrains her bow for close combat, Tanila creates sequential layered runes and plans a defensive network, and the bound demon companion learns to accept the strength shared through his bond. Rakonath begins organizing dragons into a coordinated defensive flight. Each founder is addressing a different weakness before stronger gods can reach them.

Because current divine-point growth leaves little room for failure, Max investigates a portal collective connecting dozens of worlds. Its representative offers graded arrangements ranging from trade access to full mutual defense, but unexpectedly knows about Max and Tanila's daughter. The founders choose the least binding trade partnership, intending to gain commerce while limiting disclosure and watching the network in return. The new portal raises income and opens regular traffic, yet its activation feels invasive and routes through an unidentified central Nexus. Six months later, the founders discover that the collective supports a market selling intelligence on gods. Their own profiles compile arena broadcasts, portal scans, observations, abilities, relationships, and proposed methods of isolating them. Max buys the files anonymously and learns that much of his visible arsenal is exposed, although outsiders still misunderstand Bob and underestimate important limits. The portal has solved part of the income problem while creating a systematic surveillance threat.

A peaceful tier-three shepherd god issues an anomalous challenge to Max. Investigation reveals that an ancient, overwhelming presence ordered the shepherd to enter the arena, refuse surrender, and die or see the shepherd's world destroyed. Max agrees to make the death quick and protect the world afterward. He wins the staged contest, inherits the threatened world, and discovers a large wager placed almost immediately on a short fight. The collective investigator traces similar cases, while Bob enters protected arena records and confirms seventeen connected bets from one hidden source across centuries. A vast system-adjacent presence notices the intrusion and allows Bob to retreat. Forty years pass without open retaliation, but the alliance remains far short of tier five. An arena master then offers Max a twenty-to-one wager against Unbroken, an adaptive captive undefeated against divine challengers for sixty millennia. The terms require Max to remain at tier four until combat begins.

Archives show that Unbroken has killed and absorbed seventeen tier-four challengers, learning from every attack and growing stronger after each victory. To improve income and preparation, the founders accept associate membership in the portal collective despite its greater expectations and surveillance. Merchants and organizations then approach their territories with detailed knowledge and offers carrying escalating obligations. The bound demon companion rejects a syndicate arrangement, Fowl manages trade conflict in his city, Cordelia begins counter-intelligence work, and Rakonath negotiates tightly limited trade in naturally shed dragon scales. The founders conclude that someone may be studying and positioning the entire alliance around the arena offer. Max decides that refusing will not remove the wider threat and commits to the fight after prolonged training. Bob develops True Mirror into a physical copy of Max that can fight independently, though its destruction harms Bob. The alliance mobilizes its peoples and builds tactics around Max and Bob operating as two bodies.

After decades of simulations and training, Max and Bob can sustain their two-body tactics for hours, but even their best plans leave a substantial risk of death. With one year of protection remaining, Max formally accepts the twenty-to-one wager and commits 2.5 billion divine points. The fight is scheduled only thirty days before the protective period ends. During the founders' final gathering, Fowl identifies a loophole in the contract: Max must enter at tier four, but the wording may allow Bob, who has a distinct System identity, to initiate Max's advancement once combat begins. The group keeps the plan secret because the arena might close the gap or void the wager. The rabbit-shaped helper confirms that the interpretation has a technical basis but cannot predict adjudication. Max enters the arena prepared to create a two-second opening for Bob, knowing that a successful advancement might unlock a domain while a failed ruling could cost both his life and the alliance's accumulated resources.

The System accepts Bob as the initiator of Max's advancement, making Max tier five after the fight begins. The new Consume domain needs twenty-four hours to charge, forcing Max and Bob to survive against an opponent that rapidly adapts to their weapons, magic, movement, and shared patterns. Unbroken repeatedly destroys Bob's physical clone, weakening Bob each time, while Max's mana and regeneration steadily fail. A concealed god-killing artifact wounds Unbroken but cannot overcome its adaptation. Max eventually fights without the clone, uses his remaining abilities and a mana potion to delay, and survives a lethal head strike only because Negate Death Blow activates. At the end of the twenty-four-hour countdown, Consume's domain freezes Unbroken's killing blow. Inside the domain, Unbroken is suppressed, Max's accumulated powers are amplified, and Bob is restored. Max and Bob destroy Unbroken's core, reject its offer of stolen knowledge, and absorb its essence, memories, abilities, and statistics.

The arena challenges the result, but the official who wrote the restriction confirms that it barred Max's own pre-fight advancement and deliberately left Bob's action permissible. The fifty-billion-divine-point payout therefore stands. The official also admits that the loophole was meant to give Unbroken a genuine challenge and warns that Max's victory serves other interests while attracting old enemies. Max reunites with Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, Cordelia, Rakonath, Bob, the bound demon companion, and the rabbit-shaped helper. He spends 17.5 billion divine points to become a tier-six intermediate god. Over the next week, the other six founders advance to tier five. Roughly 1.8 billion divine points remain for defenses, expansion, and reserves. The hostile syndicate has fallen silent, but Cordelia treats that as preparation rather than retreat. With about eleven months of protection left and three assault approaches still to fortify, the strengthened alliance turns immediately toward the expected attack.
